title: Integrate perf-canary synthetic probes for cross-region failover reachability + latency
creator: Miles Thornton
body:
Problem
During rehearsals and the early design phase for regional failover automation, we’ve been over-relying on service-internal signals (5xx burn, tail latency burn, capacity headroom). Those signals are necessary but not sufficient to confirm “the region is unreachable / impaired from the outside,” and we’ve seen false positives from localized service issues and telemetry gaps.

We need a small set of synthetic probes (perf-canary) that continuously validate:
- Cross-region reachability (HTTP/TCP) to public edge + internal control-plane entrypoints
- End-to-end latency (p50/p95) from multiple vantage points
- “Can a request stream connect + receive first byte” (SSE streaming handshake) as an early indicator of partial impairment

These probes feed into the Region Health Service (ENG-2413) and ultimately the failover controller’s trigger hierarchy (ADR-042).

Scope
In-scope
1) Add new perf-canary probe types and targets:
   - Public Hosted API edge: /v1/models (or lightweight authenticated endpoint) + /v1/chat/completions with minimal payload
   - Dedicated routing entrypoint (internal) for “control-plane route -> data-plane” liveness (no customer prompts; use test tenant)
   - Optional: streaming handshake probe (connect + receive headers / first chunk within budget)

2) Run probes cross-region and cross-vantage:
   - From each prod region -> every other prod region (mesh)
   - From at least two external PoPs (or cloud-runner regions) -> each prod region

3) Publish metrics suitable for ingestion by Region Health Service:
   - canary_reachability_success{src_region,dst_region,target_type} (0/1)
   - canary_rtt_ms_bucket{src_region,dst_region,target_type}
   - canary_ttfb_ms_bucket{src_region,dst_region,target_type} (where applicable)
   - canary_http_status{src_region,dst_region,target_type,status_class}

4) Provide explicit failure classification for policy evaluation:
   - “hard down” (timeout / connection failure)
   - “degraded” (TTFB/RTT above threshold)
   - “auth/config” (401/403) should page the owning team but MUST NOT trigger region failover

Out of scope
- Replacing existing SLO/burn-based alerting (ENG-2418)
- Multi-cloud synthetic providers
- Customer-specific probes for Private deployments (covered by guidance)

Design notes / constraints
- Avoid high-cardinality labels. Keep target_type in a small bounded set: {hosted_edge, hosted_stream_handshake, dedicated_router, control_plane}.
- Keep probe interval conservative (10–30s) and request payloads minimal to avoid cost.
- Use dedicated “canary tenant” credentials with read-only or constrained scopes. No customer prompts, no user data.
- Provide a static allowlist of probe destinations; do not auto-discover.
- Probes must be resilient to local runner failures; a single runner failing should not be interpreted as dst_region failure.

Acceptance criteria
- [x] New probes run in staging with mesh coverage across staging regions.
- [x] Metrics exported to the standard observability pipeline and visible in the failover signal dashboards.
- [x] Region Health Service can consume the probe stream and expose “reachability” as a first-class signal.
- [x] Alarm semantics reviewed with SRE: probe failures create clear evidence but do not on their own trigger failover without corroboration (per ADR-042).
- [x] Game day readiness: probes are running and stable at least 72h prior to the production controlled failover.

Rollout plan
1) Staging: enable all probes + validate expected baseline RTT/TTFB; inject failures by blocking egress to confirm classification.
2) Prod (shadow): enable probes with alerts in “ticket-only” mode (no paging) for 48–72h.
3) Prod: flip to paging for runner health and “auth/config” failures; keep region impairment alerts gated by Region Health Service and controller logic.

Links
- GitHub PR (perf-canary): sources/github/perf-canary/pr-188-add-cross-region-reachability-probes.json
- Related ADR: ADR-042 failover trigger signal hierarchy
- Downstream consumer: ENG-2413 Region Health Aggregator Service
- Observability + alerts: ENG-2418

Owner notes
Primary owner: Emily Zhao (Cross-region connectivity)
Reviewers: Victor Alvarez (Network), Allison Grant (Observability), Ravi Menon (Routing policy)

Risks / mitigations
- Risk: probes create alert noise during transient internet routing blips.
  Mitigation: use dampening (e.g., 3/5 failures) and corroborate with at least one in-region runner.
- Risk: probes accidentally exercise expensive models or long generations.
  Mitigation: use a lightweight endpoint or minimal token limit; enforce hard timeouts; do not request large generations.
- Risk: auth token rotation breaks probes.
  Mitigation: integrate with existing secret rotation; add distinct “auth/config” failure classification + alert.
comments: 2026-01-07 (Victor Alvarez): Please make sure the “external PoP” runners are not all in the same cloud region. We’ve been burned when the provider has a partial edge impairment. Even two distinct locations helps. Also, classify NXDOMAIN separately from connect timeout (DNS misconfig vs reachability).

2026-01-09 (Allison Grant): Metric label review: keep dst_region + src_region, but do NOT add full URL/path as a label. target_type is enough. For HTTP status, status_class only (2xx/3xx/4xx/5xx). We can log full status in exemplars if needed.

2026-01-12 (Emily Zhao): Implemented HTTP reachability + RTT probes in perf-canary. Added initial targets for hosted_edge and control_plane. Streaming handshake probe pending—need to decide if we can reliably measure first chunk without parsing the stream body.

2026-01-14 (Ravi Menon): For controller use, we mainly need an authoritative “reachability” boolean and a bounded “degraded” classification. Latency values are useful for dashboards but the decision engine should consume a summarized health state from Region Health Service.

2026-01-18 (Emily Zhao): Added streaming handshake probe as “connect + headers received within 800ms” (staging). Using test tenant + minimal request body. Added explicit failure class: auth_config, dns_error, connect_timeout, http_5xx, slow_ttfb.

2026-01-22 (Miles Thornton): Confirmed with SRE: probe failures alone will not flip routing. They provide corroboration for reachability > 5xx burn precedence in ADR-042. Please ensure Region Health Service ingest path includes a runner quorum check.

2026-02-03 (Emily Zhao): Merged perf-canary PR-188. Staging running clean for 5 days. Prod shadow enablement completed; observed a small number of dns_error from one external runner—fixed resolver config and added runner_health metric to avoid mis-attributing dst failures.
2026-02-06 (Sean Gallagher): Marking Done. Probes are stable and present on failover signal dashboards. Good to proceed with next game day with these as corroboration signals.
